ex: We have asked for a meeting and we are awaiting a response.

evaluate

(verb). Đánh giá

ex: We shall need to evaluate how the new material stands up to wear and tear.

monitor

(verb). GIám sát

ex: The nurse is monitoring his heart rate and respiration.

subconscious

(adjective). tiềm thức

Ex: Many advertisements work at a subconscious level.

pattern

(noun). Khuôn mẫu

ex: She stared at a flower pattern on the wall

Neuroscientist

(noun). bác sĩ khoa thần kinh

ex: Neuroscientists are able to record the firing of a single nerve cell.

medial

(adjective). trung gian

ex: With three people standing in a line, the person in the middle of the line has a medial position.

prefrontal

(adjective). trước trán

ex: Synapses are lost during aging in the primate prefrontal cortex.

cortex

(noun). vỏ não

ex: The cortex of a young stem is usually green

Broaden

(verb). mở rộng

ex: They say that travel broadens the mind.

neuromarketing

(noun). tiếp thị thần kinh

ex: In the emerging field of neuromarketing, researchers study the human brain's decisionmaking processes

pilot

(adjective). dẫn đầu

ex: If the pilot scheme is successful, many more homes will be offered the new television service.

collaborate

(verb). Phối hợp

ex: Two writers collaborated on the script for the film.

controversially

(adverb). một cách gây tranh cãi

ex: the horse was controversially disqualified from first place

political

(adjective). chính trị

ex: He rose quickly through the political hierarchy to become party leader.

commercial

(adjective). mang tính thương mại

ex: The commercial future of the company looks very promising.

technique

(noun). Kĩ thuật

ex: We learned some techniques for relieving stress.

institution

(noun). Tổ chức, viện

ex: The laundress at the Perkins Institution secretly carried her off to give her a bath

obsession

(noun). cuồng tín

ex: However, this knowledge is not sufficient to enable them to stop the obsessions and compulsions.’ It can, however, be used as a pry bar to keep one from obsession if wielded in a certain way

lump

(noun). cục u

ex: Check your breasts for lumps every month.

trait

(noun). đặc điểm

ex: he was a letterofthelaw man, a common trait among coaches

large-scale

(adjective). quy mô lớn

ex: They are preparing for war on a large scale.

reliable

(adjective). đáng tin cậy

ex: We are looking for someone who is reliable and hardworking.

survey

(noun). sự khảo sát, nghiên cứu

ex: the author provides a survey of the relevant literature

flawed

(adjective). có sai sót

ex: I'm flawed, but I will do my best

steer

(verb). chỉ đạo

ex: He'd watched Sean subtly steer people away from it

pollster

(noun). người thăm dò ý kiến

ex: It did prompt one wellknown internet pollster to ask its panel to compare politicians with animals.

experiment

(noun). thử nghiệm

ex: I have tested this by experiment

investigate

(verb). Điều tra

ex: Police are investigating allegations of corruption involving senior executives.

unpublished

(adjective). chưa xuất bản

ex: the archive contains much unpublished material

attitude

(noun). Thái độ

ex: It's often very difficult to change people's attitudes.

ventral

(adjective). thuộc về phần bụng

ex: The right ventricle occupies the ventral portion of the heart

putamen

(noun). hạch

ex: The scientists found that a brain region called the ventral putamen lit up most strongly when people drank their favorite cola

outweigh

(verb). đo ván, vượt qua

ex: the advantages greatly outweigh the disadvantages

profitable

(adjective). mang lại nhiều lợi nhuận

ex: I'm trying to make this a profitable business

unconscious

(adjective). bất tỉnh

ex: He was unconscious and lay like a distorted corpse

utilize

(verb). Tận dụng

ex: The vitamins come in a form that is easily utilized by the body.

introspection

(noun). nội tâm

ex: In the Midwest, introspection is practically forbidden.

fortune

(noun). Tiền của, thời vận

ex: She inherited a fortune from her grandmother.

exploitation

(noun). khai thác

ex: It was an exploitation of the patented invention

benign

(adjective). nhẹ nhàng

ex: Polymyalgia is not a benign disease, but correctly treated it can be controlled

bound

(noun). đầy đủ

ex: Townspeople of all ages have taken part in the historic beating of the bounds tradition to observe the boundaries of Malmesbury.

pathology

(noun). bệnh lý

Ex: Pathology is the study of the causes and effects of disease or injury.

implicate

(verb). liên lụy

Ex: He tried to avoid saying anything that would implicate him further.

epidemic

(noun). Đại dịch

ex: a flu epidemic is happening

obesity

(noun). béo phì

ex: Earlier it was seen as a sign of health and wealth, now obesity is a sign of poor health and poverty.’

amplify

(verb). phóng đại

ex: If you already have a large amount of productivity, technology will amplify it

decent

(adjective). Chấp nhận được

ex: I need a decent night's sleep.

subsidy

(noun). trợ cấp

ex: The company received a substantial government subsidy.

critic

(noun). nhà phê bình

ex: Her critics say she is leading the party to disaster.

particular

(adjective). cụ thể

ex: He wouldn't take just any book he had to have this particular one!

clue

(noun). manh mối

ex: He had given no clue that he was going to leave

researcher

(noun). researcher

ex: European researchers say olive oil could help prevent cancer.

disease

(noun). Căn bệnh, dịch bệnh

ex: They reported a sudden outbreak of the disease in the south of the country.

inhabitant

(noun). Cư dân

ex: it's a city of five million inhabitants

priest

(noun). thầy tu

ex: Classes were taught by the Jesuit priests and brothers and a few civilian instructors.

heap

(noun). đống

Ex: His clothes lay in a heap on the floor.

ruinous

(adjective). hư nát

ex: The buildings were in a ruinous state.

boast

(verb). Khoe khoang

ex: He didn't talk about his exam results in case people thought he was boasting.

vegetation

(noun). Thảm thực vật

ex: The railway track will have to be cleared of vegetation if it is to be used again.

unique

(adjective). đặc biệt, độc nhất

ex: I'd recognize your handwriting anywhere it's unique.

fern

(noun). cây dương xỉ

ex: The flowering plants, also known as angiosperms, Angiospermae or Magnoliophyta, are the most diverse group of land plants.

brief

(adjective). Ngắn gọn

ex: She gave us a brief instruction

conclude

(verb). Kết luận

ex: Before I conclude, I'd like to thank you all for coming.

calamity

(noun). thiên tai

ex: His financial help saved the magazine from total calamity.

denude

(verb). Lột trần quần áo, vỏ ngoài...; làm trần trụi, làm tróc vỏ, làm rụng lá

ex: The countryside has been denuded by war.

sailor

(noun). Thủy thủ

ex: He was a young sailor on his first sea voyage.

ambitious

(adjective). Đầy tham vọng

ex: She was ambitious, driven by her need for power.

scheme

(noun). Kế hoạch

ex: Under the current marking/mark scheme, you need 90 percent to get an A.

shrub

(noun). cây bụi

ex: She planted some roses and other flowering shrubs.

rainfall

(noun). sư đổ mưa

ex: The average annual rainfall in this region is 750 mm.

stimulate

(verb). Kích thích

ex: The economy was not stimulated by the tax cuts

ecological

(adjective). Liên quan đến hệ sinh thái

ex: The destruction of the rain forests is an ecological disaster.

naval

(adjective). hải quân

ex: The town has a long history as a naval port.

seedling

(noun). cây giống

ex: I wanted to plant out my lettuce seedlings, since they were too large to continue indoors.

bamboo

(noun). cây tre

ex: In her garden she has bamboos, wonderful rare tree ferns, palm trees and bananas

prickly pear

(noun). Lê gai

ex: Cacti, including prickly pear were common in lower areas.

assess

(verb). đánh giá

ex: It's difficult to assess the effects of these changes.

appeal

(verb). thu hút

ex: They're appealing for clothes and blankets to send to the devastated region.

magnetic

(adjective). từ tính

ex: The iron has lost its magnetic force

resonance

(noun). cộng hưởng

ex: The deep resonance of his voice brings out both the wisdom and intimacy of his poems.

fusion

(noun). dấu tích

Ex: The movie displayed a perfect fusion of image and sound.

inevitably

(adverb). Không tránh khỏi

ex: When Kim and I fought, I would inevitably retreat into the safety of my irony cage

advocate

(noun). Người biện hộ, người bào chữa, người bênh vực; luật sư, thầy cãi

ex: He got the best advocate in town to defend him

invasion

(noun). Sự đánh giá

ex: One of the more insidious invasions of our privacy rights is the rampant spread of drug tests in the American workplace.

misuse

(verb). lạm dụng

ex: She was accused of misusing company funds.

implausible

(adjective). có vẻ không thật

ex: Her explanation is not implausible.

frivolous

(adjective). Thiếu kiên nhẫn

Ex: Sorry, I was being frivolous.

sections.title: Passage 3: The accidental rainforest
sections.html:
conservationist

(noun). A person who advocates or acts for the protection and preservation of the environment

ex: The decision to become a wildlife conservationist was accidental.

ecologist

(noun). An expert in or student of ecology.

ex: And unless current trends reverse, ecologists predict the last rainforest tree will fall in the next 40 years.

anarchy

(noun). a situation in a country, an organization, etc. in which there is no government, order or control

Ex: The overthrow of the military regime was followed by a period of anarchy.

exotic

(adjective). originating in or characteristic of a distant foreign country.

Ex: Even the eighteenth century British art is looking strikingly exotic.

indigenous

(adjective). Originating or occurring naturally in a particular place

ex: The most indigenous inhabitants were the American Indians

endemic

(adjective). regularly found among particular people or in a certain are

ex: Parasitic infections are endemic among this population

coexist

(verb). exist at the same time or in the same place.

ex: The two communities coexist peacefully.

rainforest

(noun). a thick forest in tropical parts of the world that have a lot of rain

ex: This humid subtropical rainforest covers about 90% of the park.

tropical

(adjective). Of, typical of, or peculiar to the tropics.

ex: The slow ceiling fans made little impact against the tropical heat.

constituent

(noun). a member of a constituency.

ex: What are the basic constituents of the mixture?

complex

(adjective). Consisting of many different and connected parts

ex: The company has a complex organizational structure.

emerge

(verb). move out of way and become visible

ex: She emerged from the sea, blue with cold.

niche

(noun). a shallow recess, especially one in a wall to display a statue or other ornament

ex: her bed was tucked into a niche in the wall

pollinator

(noun). something, such as an insect, that carries pollen from one plant or part of a plant to another

Ex: These chemicals are known to be highly toxic to honeybees and other pollinators.

disperser

(noun). a type of mixer used to rapidly break apart lumps of powdery material, uniformly distributing and wetting them in a liquid.

Ex: A Disperser is a single shaft mixer used to break apart or dissolve solid particles in a liquid.

microbe

(noun). a microorganism, especially a bacterium causing disease or fermentation.

ex: The microbe does not form spores within the animal body

evolve

(verb). develop gradually and in distinct stages

ex: Did humans evolve from apes?

evolutionary

(adjective). connected with evolution; connected with gradual development and change

ex: The change has been evolutionary rather than revolutionary.

framework

(noun). A basic structure underlying a system, concept, or text

ex: The report provides a framework for further research

ecosystem

(noun). a biological community of interacting organisms and their physical environment

ex: Pollution can have disastrous effects on the delicately balanced ecosystem.

adornment

(noun). a thing which adorns or decorates; an ornament

ex: Her room doesnt have any unnecessary adornments.

structural

(adjective). relating to or forming part of the structure of a building or other item.

ex: Hundreds of houses in the typhoons path suffered structural damage.

instant

(adjective). happening or coming immediately.

ex: Contrary to expectations, the film was an instant success.

plausible

(adjective). eeming reasonable or probable >< unreasonable, improbable (không có khả năng)

ex: She could find no plausible explanation for its disappearance

supposedly

(adverb). According to what is generally assumed or believed à seemingly, apparently

ex: Well, the tickets are supposedly in the mail.

pristine

(adjective). In its original condition

ex: My office is a mess but her office is always pristine.

civilisation

(noun). a state of human society that is very developed and organized

ex: Some people think that nuclear war would mean the end of civilization.

authority

(noun). A person or organization having political or administrative power and control

ex: Now he was exerting his authority in another way.

misguided

(adjective). wrong because you have understood or judged a situation badly

ex: He blames the crisis on the governments misguided economic policies.

extinct

(adjective). (of a species, family, or other larger group) having no living members

ex: There is concern that the giant panda will soon become extinct.

urgency

(noun). Importance requiring swift action

ex: She stressed the urgency of an early solution.

enigma

(noun). a person, thing or situation that is mysterious and difficult to understand

Ex: Even after years he still remains an enigma to me

chunk

(noun). a thick solid piece that has been cut or broken off something

ex: huge chunks of masonry littered the street

caterpillar

(noun). a small creature like a worm with legs, that develops into a butterfly or moth (= flying insects with large, sometimes brightly coloured, wings)

ex: Caterpillars eat the leaves of plants.

beetle

(noun). an insect, often large and black, with a hard case on its back, covering its wings

ex: Dung beetles are beetles that feed partly or exclusively on feces (dung).

feature

(noun). a distinctive attribute or aspect of something.

ex: Our latest model of phone has several new features.

artificial

(adjective). made or produced to copy something natural; not real

ex: All things are artificial, for nature is the art of God.

interfere

(verb). take part or intervene in an activity without invitation or necessity

ex: The authorities did not interfere with us

slope

(noun). an area of land that is part of a mountain or hill

ex: hey waited until he climbed up the slope to where they stood

shrub

(noun). a woody plant which is smaller than a tree and has several main stems arising at or near the ground

ex: She planted some roses and other flowering shrubs.

roaring success

(noun). a very great success

ex: The theatre is a roaring success in this country

reconsider

(verb). consider (something) again, especially for a possible change of decision regarding it.

ex: She refused to reconsider her decision not to loan us the money.

fern

(noun). a plant with large delicate leaves and no flowers that grows in wet areas or is grown in a pot. There are many types of fern

ex: Growing a fern is a great start to learning how to lok after your garden

trigger

(verb). cause (an event or situation) to happen or exist

ex: Some people find that certain foods trigger their headaches.

garrison

(noun). a group of soldiers living in a town or fort to defend it; the buildings these soldiers live in

Ex: Half the garrison is/are on duty.

packet

(noun). a small paper or cardboard container in which goods are packed for selling

ex: It will be cheaper to send it as a small packet.

cloak

(verb). to cover or hide something

ex: He has always kept his love affairs cloaked in secrecy

prolific

(adjective). producing much fruit or foliage or many offspring.

ex: Rabbits and other rodents are prolific (= have a lot of babies).

sparse

(adjective). only present in small amounts or numbers and often spread over a large area

ex: It is a wellwooded tract, in many places stretching out in charming glades like an English park, but it has a very sparse population

luxuriant

(adjective). growing thickly and strongly in a way that is attractive

ex: Tall, luxuriant plants grew along the river bank.

tenet

(noun). one of the principles on which a belief or theory is based

ex: A major tenet of the womens movement has been that society needs their talents.

ragbag

(noun). a collection of things that appear to have little connection with each other

ex: Heavy snow has caused total chaos on the roads.

proper

(adjective). of the required type; suitable or appropriate

ex: He is always perfectly proper in his behavior

characterise

(verb). describe the distinctive nature or features of.

ex: Bright colours and bold strokes characterize his early paintings.

invasive

(adjective). spreading very quickly and difficult to stop

ex: They treated the cancer with noninvasive methods/surgery

earmark

(verb). to decide that something will be used for a particular purpose, or to state that something will happen to somebody/something in the future

ex: Five billion dollars of this years budget is already earmarked for hospital improvements.

irony

(noun). the amusing or strange aspect of a situation that is very different from what you expect; a situation like this

ex: The irony (of it) is that the new tax system will burden those it was intended to help.
